pageCache.pageTitle: Bussage C of E Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Learning for life in all its fullness
Latest News
Welcome to our school
Welcome to Bussage Church of England Primary School, near the historic Gloucestershire market town of Stroud. We are a one form entry Primary School with around 210 pupils and cater for children in and around the Parish of Bussage with Eastcombe aged 4-11. Our ethos and vision is to provide an exciting and stimulating education underpinned by Christian values. We look to instil in our children all the skills to become independent lifelong learners to prepare them well for their next stage of education.
Ofsted Says
Pupils are keen to learn and behave well. They are polite and respectful. The school is a purposeful place to learn. Pupils are not afraid to make mistakes in their learning. They form strong relationships with their peers and with adults. Ofsted, 2022
New Parents say:
"I was nervous about the transition to primary school as my son had previously only been to nursery 2 days a week. However, he was so well supported by the staff at school that by his third week he was telling me how much he loved Rainbows and was keen to go every morning.
Since then he has continued to love going to school and has really grown in confidence. He comes home and tells us about what he’s been learning and asks to practice his phonics and maths. He particularly loves PEG time in Rainbows where children can follow their own interests, as well as the Forest School and PE lessons. Mrs Bennett and the support staff in Rainbows are wonderful and he is very fond of all of them, and we feel confident he is being well cared for each day.
The most important thing for me is that he is always happy to go to school and talks positively about his day there, and therefore I am so glad we chose Bussage."
Open Mornings:
Come and see what makes us unique - contact the school office to book your place 01453 883205 admin@bussage.gloucs.sch.uk
Did you know you can also book our upcoming Forest School session for pre-schoolers on Thursday 5th November 9:30-10:30 am and to come and see our Nativity dress rehearsal with your pre-school child on Monday 7th December 9:45 am.
We would love to see you!
Thursday 12th November at 9.30am
Wednesday 2nd December 9:30am

pageCache.pageTitle: Bussage C of E Primary School - Our Vision & Values
pageCache.text:
Our Vision & Values
Learning for life in all its fullness
At Bussage C of E Primary School, our mission is to provide a learning and development environment in which all pupils and staff can flourish. We welcome families of all faiths, or none, into our school and are incredibly proud of the welcoming and inclusive nature of our community. Our thematic, creative curriculum has been designed to encourage every child to make the most of their potential and aspire to be the best that they can be. Our school is one in which children can learn safely with guidance, support, a strong sense of community and a broad awareness of, and sensitivity to, their environment and society.
The theology underpinning our vision, "I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full."(John 10:10)
is central to the formation of our curriculum which has been designed to develop ‘the whole child’. Put simply, we want all our children to experience all that the world has to offer, to know their importance within it and to be a shining example of all that is good. We guide them to recognise the light that their talents, gifts, character and acts of kindness can shine into the world, making it a better place for all those around them.
SIAMS inspection report Autumn 2024
We are delighted to share our SIAMS (Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools) inspection report with you all.
Some of the highlights from this report are:
'Bussage C of E Primary School is living up to its foundation as a Church school and is enabling pupils and adults to flourish. It has the following notable strengths.'
'A strong sense of community binds everyone together leading to flourishing.'
'A clear vision of learning for life in all its fullness is lived in this community. This leads to a culture of exemplary care for the wide range of needs in the school.'
'Pupils make a difference in this school.'
The school is 'a beacon of light on the hill'.
This report draws together the wonderful community that Bussage C of E Primary School is, and truly reflects the ethos and culture of the school.
SIAMS Inspection report 2024
Our Christian Values
Our vision and Christian values are at the heart of everything we do. They underpin our teaching and learning and provide an environment which prepares our pupils to leave our setting as confident, happy individuals who live life to the full.
We reflect and focus on 12 Christian Values over a period of 2 years. Please find parent/home sheets linked below to each of our values for your use.
Autumn 1 - Generosity
Autumn 2 - Compassion
Spring 2 - Forgiveness
Summer 1 - Friendship
Autumn 1 - ThankfulnessAutumn 2 - TrustSpring 1 - PerseveranceSpring 2 - JusticeSummer 1- ServiceSummer 2 - TruthfulnessWell-being is valued across the school and we encourage mindfulness to allow pupils the time to reflect upon their spiritual development. Teachers recognise the importance of giving time to pause and think throughout the school day. Staff have received spirituality training from the diocese and have fully embedded the use of OWs, WOWs and NOWs across the school.
The Ows
These are the things that can go wrong. They can knock the breath out of you.
The Wows
These are the awe and wonder moments. The times when you want to breathe in and capture the feeling, holding onto it as long as you can.
The Nows
These are the everyday ordinary times. Thinking of what we have now and how lucky we are to be here, now.
Our newly refurbished ‘Tranquility Garden’ gives children a calm and inviting space to reflect on their spirituality, pray or take a mindful moment in the midst of a busy school day. We are incredibly fortunate to have such a wonderful outdoor space for our children to use both with their class and during break times.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bussage C of E Primary School - British Values
pageCache.text:
British Values at Bussage C of E Primary School
Living Out Our Vision:“Learning for Life in All Its Fullness” (John 10:10)
At Bussage C of E Primary School, British Values are woven into the daily life of our school and sit naturally alongside our Christian vision and values of Wisdom, Hope, Community and Dignity. We believe that every child should flourish academically, socially, spiritually and emotionally, enabling them to become thoughtful, responsible and compassionate citizens who make a positive difference in the world. Our vision encourages children to recognise the light within themselves and others and to use their gifts, talents and character to contribute positively to society.
The Department for Education identifies the fundamental British Values as:
These values are promoted explicitly through our curriculum, collective worship, School Parliament, wellbeing curriculum, wider enrichment opportunities and everyday interactions across our school community.
Democracy
The Rule of Law
Individual Liberty
Mutual Respect
Democracy
At Bussage, children are encouraged to understand that their voices matter and that everyone has the right to contribute to decisions affecting their community. Democracy is embedded throughout school life and reflects our commitment to developing pupils who can participate confidently and respectfully in society.
The most visible example of democracy in action is our School Parliament, where children are elected by their peers through a democratic voting process. Candidates prepare speeches, share their ideas and campaign for election before secret ballots are held. Through this experience, pupils learn about representation, fairness and accountability.
Our School Parliament is organised into five ministries, led by Year 6 pupils and supported by staff members. These ministries develop action plans, lead projects and report back to the wider school community throughout the year. This reflects our belief that pupils can make a genuine difference within school, their local community and the wider world. The school's recent SIAMS inspection recognised that"Pupils make a difference in this school."
Children are also consulted through:
By encouraging pupils to express their views and listen carefully to others, we help them develop the wisdom and confidence required to participate positively in modern Britain.
Termly pupil conferencing sessions
Wellbeing and curriculum questionnaires
Suggestion boxes
Collective worship reflections

School Parliament campaign posters and election speeches.
The Rule of Law
At Bussage, we help children understand that rules and laws are essential in creating safe, caring and successful communities. Through our vision of dignity and community, children learn that rules exist to protect everyone's rights and freedoms.
Our three school rules:
provide a simple and consistent framework that helps children make positive choices. At the beginning of each school year, classes explore what these rules mean in practice and how they help everyone flourish.
Children learn about laws and responsibilities through our curriculum, collective worship, history learning, visits from community services and discussions about fairness, justice and responsibility. We support children in understanding not only the consequences of poor choices but also the positive impact they can have through making good ones.
Be Ready
Be Respectful
Be Safe

Individual Liberty
Our vision encourages every child to discover their God-given talents and develop confidence in who they are. We believe that children flourish when they are given opportunities to make choices, take responsibility and develop independence within safe boundaries.
Children are taught about rights, responsibilities and personal freedoms through our wellbeing curriculum, online safety education, worship and wider curriculum experiences. We encourage pupils to develop their own interests, opinions and aspirations while understanding that liberty comes with responsibility toward others.
Pupils regularly make choices about:
We encourage children to develop their talents, make responsible choices and discover their unique gifts as part of living life in all its fullness
Our nurturing environment helps children develop resilience, confidence and self-belief whilst ensuring they understand how to exercise their freedoms safely and respectfully.

Mutual Respect
Mutual respect lies at the heart of our Christian vision and is reflected in our commitment to dignity for every member of our school community. We actively model and teach respect through all aspects of school life.
Christmas boxes created and collected at school ready to be sent off to Eastern Europe to children who are in need of our support.
Children learn that everyone is unique and valued. They understand that respectful relationships help communities thrive and that their words and actions can positively affect those around them.
Our welcoming and inclusive ethos enables children to build strong relationships with peers and adults. This is reflected in the school's positive culture, recognised by both Ofsted and SIAMS. Ofsted noted that pupils are "polite and respectful" and that the school feels like a family.
Examples of Children's Work
Collaborative learning projects demonstrating teamwork and cooperation.
Peer support and buddy activities, peer mentoring.
Tolerance and Understanding of Different Faiths and Beliefs
As a Church of England school, we welcome families of all faiths and of no faith and are proud of our inclusive community. Our vision of community encourages children to understand, respect and celebrate differences while recognising what unites us.
Through our Religion and Worldviews curriculum, collective worship and wider curriculum opportunities, pupils learn about Christianity and a range of world faiths and beliefs. They explore different traditions, values and ways of life, helping them develop empathy, understanding and respect.
Children are encouraged to ask questions, challenge stereotypes and engage thoughtfully with different perspectives. We celebrate cultural diversity and help pupils understand their role as respectful global citizens.
Examples of Children's Work
Reflections following visits to places of worship.
Challenging Discrimination and Extremism
Bussage C of E Primary School is committed to creating a safe, inclusive and respectful environment for all. We actively challenge discrimination, prejudice and any views that undermine the fundamental British Values of democracy, liberty, respect, tolerance and the rule of law.
Through our curriculum, worship and relationships-based approach, we equip children with the knowledge, confidence and critical thinking skills needed to recognise and challenge intolerance and extremism. We encourage pupils to be courageous advocates who stand up for what is right and contribute positively to society.
By living out our vision of"Learning for Life in All Its Fullness", we prepare children to become compassionate, confident and responsible citizens who embody the values of Wisdom, Hope, Community and Dignity in everything they do.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bussage C of E Primary School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
A very warm welcome to Bussage C of E Primary School. We are situated in the village of Bussage, on the top of a hill with stunning countryside and views. Bussage is a village of rural background and is close to the historic market town of Stroud, which lies below the western escarpment of the Cotswold Hills in an area of beauty. Our school is single form entry for ages 4 – 11 and can accommodate up to 210 pupils. Our children join us largely from the surrounding areas of Bussage, Eastcombe and Chalford. We offer wrap around care in the form of a Breakfast Club, which runs from 7:45 am daily; and an After School Club which runs until 5:15pm Monday to Thursday and until 4:15pm on a Friday. We have beautiful extensive grounds inclusive of a wild classroom forest school area, a tranquility garden, trim trail, adventure playground and musical playground.
Ofsted October 2022
Pupils are keen to learn and behave well. They are polite and respectful.
The school is a purposeful place to learn. Pupils are not afraid to make mistakes in their learning. They form strong relationships with their peers and with adults.
Children, parents and carers and staff love this school.
Bussage Church of England Primary School continues to be a GOOD SCHOOL.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bussage C of E Primary School - About Us
pageCache.text:
About Us
Welcome to Bussage Primary School.
Bussage is a Church of England Aided Primary School, which caters for pupils aged 4 – 11 years.
We deliver a well-researched curriculum with committed staff led by the Headteacher. As well as gaining language, mathematical, scientific and technological skills, your child will develop in confidence, become more self-reliant, learn decision making and develop the ability to articulate feelings and ideas. Socially, we seek to enable children to build relationships with others, and be sensitive to the feelings and needs of those around them.
We feel that your involvement in the process of your child’s education is crucial and we will keep you informed on how your child is progressing. We are very keen to encourage parental involvement at all levels – you will be made very welcome if you have any spare time to help in classrooms, or any ideas for improvements.
We all agree that childhood experiences at Primary level are very important. We will do our best to make it as enjoyable and productive as possible for your child during their education here at Bussage School.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bussage C of E Primary School - Headteacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Our school is a special place that prides itself on being a happy school where children and adults are encouraged to have a caring, considerate and respectful attitude towards one another. Sharing special moments together and building a lifetime love for learning, our children learn to challenge themselves and know how to take risks to deepen their understanding. Within a Christian ethos, we recognise the value and uniqueness of every child, helping all to flourish within a safe, secure and nurturing environment. This is done through meaningful opportunities that are relevant to the children’s needs both now and in years to come.
Our strong vision enables our children, staff and community to develop a love of learning, a spirit of enquiry and a determination to succeed. We promote active learning through an engaging and creative thematic curriculum. Our pupils benefit from high quality teaching and learning experiences, a wide range of enrichment opportunities, a broad, balanced and exciting curriculum all within a vibrant Christian learning environment. We place value on enjoyment of reading and the pleasure that can be gained by reading or sharing a book.
Enjoy exploring and discovering all we have to offer. We love our school and hope you will too. The website gives you just a glimpse, you are warmly invited to visit us to find out more about our wonderful school.
Mrs Zoe White - Headteacher
